observations: Files I actually read: the request JSON (requiredTransitions and the recorded first reading; I took the page 02 panel script from the identical boundary context in the page 01 request and the page 03 request), source/original.txt and source/REVISION-2026-11-11.md. I opened these images with Read and looked at them: workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-02.png, workflow/storyboards/page-02.png, workflow/review/page-02.png and assets/panels/02-4.png. I grepped the text and the teal label rects of storyboards-unnumbered/page-02.svg and the beat text of storyboards/page-02.svg. No file was unreadable.

The PNGs match the SVGs. The SVG text runs are 'The clinic begins its / Welbuk / onboarding.', 'WELBUK PRACTICE / for the / clinic', 'We can organise our / clinic workflow here.', 'And our team can / use tools suited / to each staff role.', 'WELBUK CARE / for clinic staff' and 'One team. / Better / coordination.'. The teal label rects are at (706,24,294x138) and (664,968,234x106), which matches the image. The numbered PNG adds only the beat footers. In 02-3 the footer '3 / Meera discovers Welbuk Care for staff' is partly overlapped by the WELBUK CARE label, but it is an internal storyboard annotation and is not in the final.

The script matches the source, page 2 panels 1-4. The caption and all three dialogue lines are verbatim, with the source's speakers (Ananya, Meera, Ananya). The two product labels are manga supplements that name the products shown in the source ('Welbuk Practice' on the laptop and 'Welbuk Care' on the staff phone).

Meera's 'And our team can...' continues Ananya's 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' as an additive second point ('And'). The referent of 'here' is the laptop shown in 02-1 and 02-2. 'One team. Better coordination.' sums up both points. No reply depends on a removed line.

Unnumbered scan: the top-left caption, then the top-right WELBUK PRACTICE label. Next, Ananya's balloon at the top left of the middle-left panel, then Meera's balloon at the top of the middle-right panel with the WELBUK CARE label below it. The bottom tier has one centred balloon. Each panel has at most one balloon, so there are no proximity clusters that could cause a skipped reply.

First-reader concern 1: the caption and the WELBUK PRACTICE label are flush with the panel frame. In the composed preview the caption is a square corner box fitted into the top-left corner, and 'its' clears the box's right edge with a small margin. The label fills the top-right corner over the evening window and does not touch Ananya's face, hands or the laptop screen. It is a cosmetic corner-box placement with no effect on reading, and it is legible at page size. I accept it.

First-reader concerns 2 and 3: in 02-4 the balloon cuts off the 'ananya' placeholder name, and a reader might attribute the line to Meera. In the preview and in assets/panels/02-4.png, the balloon sits in the wall area between the two women. Its short tail enters from the right at Ananya's open, smiling mouth, and her raised encouraging fist matches 'One team.'. Meera, at the right, has a closed-mouth smile and is listening. The balloon covers neither face. The placeholder overlap exists only in the storyboard, and the art and preview show the attribution clearly.

02-3: in the preview the WELBUK CARE label covers the desk and laptop corner below Meera. It is clear of her face and of the protected phone region (794,794,40,61), and the phone screen with the calendar icon stays visible.

transitions.observation: Ananya says 'Let's make the rest simpler' in the morning reception. Then the caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' appears over an over-the-shoulder evening shot of Ananya typing into a blank setup form. The caption plus the sunset window mark the time and place change (02-1 transition: time-change), and the decision on page 1 is followed by the action.

The same office, evening light, laptop and coat. 02-2 moves from typing to a seated three-quarter view, with a finger at her chin and her gaze up and away, as she speaks about organising the workflow. The action continues directly.

02-3 shows Meera standing by the desk with the staff phone and the open laptop beside her, in the same evening window light. 'And our team...' adds to Ananya's line. Meera's entrance is not shown, but the shared office and her direct continuation make it clear that she is with Ananya.
A two-shot brings them together: Ananya seated at the left, Meera standing at the right with the same phone at her side, and the laptop between them. Ananya's summary line follows Meera's point.

The evening two-shot is followed by page 3's caption 'A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk.' over a bright reception. The page 03 SVG and preview show daylight and a tidy desk. The time change is stated in the caption (03-1 transition: time-change).

readingReview.comparison: My comparison agrees with the recorded first reading's order: caption, label, Ananya, Meera with the label, then the closing line, which is the intended [1,2],[1],[1,2],[1]. The first reader saw no skipped reply, and I agree. Its four layout notes are resolved as follows. (1) The flush caption and label are a cosmetic corner placement that stays legible in the preview, so I accept them. (2) and (3) The balloon overlapping the ananya placeholder and the possible attribution to Meera exist only in the placeholder. In the preview and accepted art the tail goes to Ananya's speaking mouth, Meera is a silent listener, and no face is covered. (4) The page 1 to page 2 transition is understandable, and I agree. Nothing is left unresolved.
